notes: [family: Globe Swift] Right side of canopy separated at 150-200 ft on takeoff climb; pilot believed front canopy pin engaged (visually checked) but rear pin found outside; findings: canopy separation + preflight inadequate; hard landing after tight turn to final. [date from report Date & Time field; ELMIRA, New York]

[family: Rutan EZ] Witness saw canopy come open in initial climb; spin entered while pilot tried to close it. Findings: canopy UNLOCKED (F), preflight inadequate (C), diverted attention (C). [date from report Date & Time field; RED BLUFF, California]

[family: Taylor Coot] Second flight after an earlier hard landing; canopy came open on base leg; aircraft stalled/spun while pilot tried to close it. No canopy cause stated. [date from report Date & Time field; PUNTA GORDA, Florida]

[family: PIK-20] Canopy opened during takeoff roll; glider climbed to ~10 ft then descended nose-low. Finding: preflight planning/preparation inadequate (cause of opening not stated explicitly). [date from report Date & Time field; MINDEN, Nevada]

[family: Wing Derringer] Canopy came open; pilot held it closed during emergency landing, struck ground 100 ft short. Findings: canopy UNLOCKED (F), preflight improper (C). [date from report Date & Time field; BUNNELL, Florida]
[family: Bede BD-5] Witnesses and pilot: canopy opened shortly after departure; aft canopy locking pins were not engaged. [date from report Date & Time field; MERCED, California]
[family: Eagle DW-1] Pilot failed to lock cockpit canopy before takeoff roll; canopy opened and separated during the roll. [date from report Date & Time field; CORNING, Arkansas]

[family: Grob G103] On aerotow at ~250 ft glider rolled 90 deg by gust; canopy came open, opened again while pilot tried to secure it; lost sight of towplane, released at ~80 ft stalled, trees. Findings: canopy open (F). [date from report Date & Time field; LITTLE RIVER, South Carolina]

[family: Grob G102] Canopy came open after release at ~2,000 ft AGL; low airspeed on final, spin, 45 deg nose-down impact. Findings: aircraft preflight inattentive (F), canopy open (C). [date from report Date & Time field; CALIFORNIA CITY, California]
[family: Cassutt] Pilot reported he did not properly lock the canopy; it came open at 7,000 ft MSL. [date from report Date & Time field; BRIGHTON, Colorado]

[family: Moni] Canopy opened at ~12 ft AGL in initial climb; aircraft became uncontrollable, hard touchdown. Pilot stated it was closed and locked; NTSB finding: crew door/canopy UNLOCKED (C). [date from report Date & Time field; TERRELL, Texas]

[family: Cassutt] First test flight of homebuilt; canopy came open; pilot landed holding it closed, could not flare (little airflow over tail); pilot seriously injured. [date from report Date & Time field; BURNET, Texas]
[family: Bushby Mustang] Canopy suddenly separated while flying S-turns/lazy eights; landed; canopy not recovered; reason not determined. [date from report Date & Time field; UPLAND, California]

[family: Schweizer SGS] Canopy came open on aerotow; pilot tried to lock it, lost control, glider pitched up. PC: loss of control after canopy came open; contributing: failure to properly close canopy before takeoff. [date from report Date & Time field; KUTZTOWN, Pennsylvania]

[family: Vans RV] Witnesses saw pilot taxi with canopy cracked open ~2 in; soon after takeoff canopy departed with pilot's glasses; stall. PC: failure to properly latch canopy before takeoff. [date from report Date & Time field; HESPERIA, California]

[family: Grob G102] At 200 ft AGL on tow canopy snapped open and tow rope broke; pilot said closed and locked; FAA found nothing wrong with lock. PC: canopy opening for undetermined reasons. [date from report Date & Time field; MARICOPA, Arizona]

[family: Sonerai] Newly purchased homebuilt; canopy popped open after level-off; pilot held it down instead of adding power; nosed over in field. Findings: canopy NOT SECURED (F). [date from report Date & Time field; CHEROKEE, Iowa]

[family: Rand KR] Canopy attach point separated from fuselage; canopy parts ~1/2 mile from wreckage. PC: loss of control; factor: total failure of the canopy. [date from report Date & Time field; BOONE, Iowa]

[family: Zenith Zodiac] At 150 ft on short final canopy came open on the left side and separated; stall/mush. Contributing: failure to fully lock the canopy before flight. [date from report Date & Time field; LAKELAND, Florida]

[family: Grob G103] Solo student on final heard loud crack; canopy broken and open, struck pilot's face; hard landing. PC: failure of the cockpit canopy; reason not found. [date from report Date & Time field; HINCKLEY, Illinois]

[family: Grob G103] Rear canopy opened on aerotow at ~600 ft AGL; lock found serviceable. PC: loss of control while closing canopy; factor: failure to properly close canopy before takeoff. [date from report Date & Time field; FORREST CITY, Arkansas]
[family: Schweizer SGS] Canopy popped open shortly after takeoff during climb-out. Factors: canopy not secured; inadequate preflight. [date from report Date & Time field; NORTH PLAINS, Oregon]

[family: Bede BD-10] Canopy began to open after Vr; takeoff aborted. Lock pins fully extended (extinguishing the CANOPY OPEN light) but had not engaged the lugs. PC: lock-pin design gave a 'closed and locked' indication without the pin engaged. FALSE-CLOSED WARNING. [date from report Date & Time field; CHESTERFIELD, Missouri]
[family: Vans RV] Canopy opened just after liftoff; pilot aborted with insufficient runway, trees, nose-over. Findings: canopy open (F). [date from report Date & Time field; ZELLWOOD, Florida]

[family: Rominger Eyas] Canopy came open ~20 ft AGL and separated; wind blast impaired vision; hard landing. PC: inadequate builder design change to canopy; canopy malfunction. [date from report Date & Time field; SANTA ROSA, California]

[family: Homebuilt (Burns)] Pilot stated he did not lock the cockpit canopy; at ~10 ft on takeoff it came open and aircraft fell to runway. PC: failure to follow checklist and secure the canopy. [date from report Date & Time field; SITKA, Alaska]

[family: EAA Biplane] Pilot closed canopy against wind but did not lock it, still had not locked it after taxi/run-up; unsecured canopy opened in takeoff roll; loss of directional control, nose-over. Factor: no checklist. [date from report Date & Time field; WILLIAMSPORT, Pennsylvania]
[family: Schweizer SGS] Canopy suddenly opened during takeoff roll. Factors: unlatched canopy; inadequate preflight. [date from report Date & Time field; FORT WAINWRIGHT, Alaska]

[family: Zenith Zodiac] Pilot distracted during pre-departure checks and forgot to pin the canopy; it popped open at liftoff; excess drag, stall. PC: failure to follow checklist to pin canopy. [date from report Date & Time field; NAUVOO, Illinois]

[family: Grob G103] About 50 ft after takeoff rear canopy 'banged' open; pilot aborted initial climb. PC: loss of control; improper decision to abort due to open canopy. [date from report Date & Time field; WELLINGTON, Ohio]

[family: Gifford TR-4] Pilot inadvertently failed to engage the right clam-shell door (canopy) aft locking mechanism; door came open after takeoff; pilot tried to close it in flight. PC names canopy (entry door) not fully secured. [date from report Date & Time field; WENATCHEE, Washington]

[family: Aero L-39] About 30 s after takeoff, in a steep low turn, the rear-seat canopy transparency failed and separated (headset and hat went with it); divergent oscillation, impact. Factors: diverted attention due to transparency failure; aft CG. Cause of transparency failure not determined. [date from report Date & Time field; Watkins, Colorado]

[family: Interavia] Witness saw loop and rolls; fatal impact. PC: separation of the canopy for undetermined reasons (finding canopy SEPARATION, phase descent). [date from report Date & Time field; Santa Rosa Bch, Florida]

[family: Rutan EZ] Pilot: canopy not secured properly before takeoff, opened just after rotation; loss of directional control. PC: failure to secure canopy. [date from report Date & Time field; Macomb, Michigan]

[family: Rutan Defiant] One-piece canopy opened near-vertical in initial climb; pilot reduced then restored power, canopy 'bobbing'; descending turn and loss of control. Contributing: canopy opening and diverted attention. Lock state not stated. [date from report Date & Time field; Slaton, Texas]

aircraft_type: Akro Tech Aviation Inc. Giles G-300
notes: [family: Giles] Acrylic canopy separated in fragments as aircraft ascended in aerobatics; no control inputs afterwards. PC: catastrophic separation of canopy from failure of the forward canopy hinge; pilot incapacitated. [date from report Date & Time field; Yukon, Oklahoma]

[family: Sonerai] Side-opening canopy held by three 1/4-in pins with friction only, no locking mechanism; opened fully at ~500 ft AGL, aircraft became uncontrollable unless held closed. Factor: unlatched canopy. Design lacking a lock mapped mechanism_failure (R5 judgement). [date from report Date & Time field; Ashland, Kentucky]

[family: Lancair] Pilot took off with canopy not fully locked; it opened during takeoff; pitch control lost. Kit maker: flyable with canopy open. Contributing: failure to ensure canopy fully locked; canopy oscillations. [date from report Date & Time field; Longmont, Colorado]

[family: Cirrus] Gaithersburg MD. Passenger door opened 2-3 in as aircraft entered cloud at 700-1,000 ft MSL in IFR initial climb (rain, cold air, noise); spatial disorientation. Door lock mechanism had no anomalies. Contributing: pilot's failure to properly secure the door latch. Found via CAROL query door+opened+Cirrus.

[family: Liberty XL-2] Incident. Left door popped open in moderate turbulence and separated; aft locking pin not completely engaged (composite door can be torsionally deformed if pins not fully engaged). Checklist item 'CLOSED AND SECURE'. [date from report Date & Time field; Camarillo, California]

[family: Vans RV] Canopy opened on takeoff roll before liftoff; pilot partly locked it, flew pattern; it opened again in the flare. PC: failure to follow pre-takeoff checklist. [date from report Date & Time field; Sparks, Nevada]

[family: Rutan EZ] Pilot had not securely locked canopy; at ~70 mph it partly opened, canvas cover exited and damaged propeller; fire. PC: failure to securely lock canopy before takeoff. [date from report Date & Time field; Afton, Wyoming]

[family: Schempp-Hirth Cirrus] Cockpit canopy inadvertently opened while on aerotow. PC: inadvertent opening of the canopy for undetermined reasons. [date from report Date & Time field; Moriarty, New Mexico]

aircraft_type: CZECH AIRCRAFT WORKS SPOL SRO Sportcruiser
notes: [family: Czech Sportcruiser] Canopy opened in the crosswind turn shortly after takeoff; POH says do not try to close it, continue and land. PC: inadvertent opening distracted pilot; contributing: not following the manufacturer's canopy-open procedure. Lock state not stated. [date from report Date & Time field; Las Vegas, Nevada]

[family: Evektor Sportstar] Canopy opened as aircraft became airborne; pilot stated he failed to secure it; no mechanical faults. PC: attempt to secure open canopy during takeoff, loss of control, hard landing. [date from report Date & Time field; Lancaster, Pennsylvania]

[family: Evektor Sportstar] Student missed the checklist item to lock the canopy; it rattled and flapped open in the takeoff roll; continued while reaching behind head to secure it; loss of directional control. [date from report Date & Time field; Myerstown, Pennsylvania]

[family: Vans RV] Two objects that exited the cabin indicate the canopy likely opened in cruise, leading to loss of pitch control; fire precluded examination of canopy/lock. PC: loss of pitch control due to in-flight canopy opening for undetermined reasons. [date from report Date & Time field; Sauk Rapids, Minnesota]

[family: Schweizer SGS] Canopy became loose on aerotow climb-out; could not lock it, lost sight of tug, released at ~300 ft; held canopy with left hand so could not use spoilers; tree, hard landing. PC: failure to ensure canopy locked during pre-takeoff inspection. [date from report Date & Time field; Marana, Arizona]

[family: Ackland SH-3R] At ~80 kt canopy handle vibrated to the open position and canopy opened; aborted takeoff; landing gear retracted (mis-installed switch). Handle movement by vibration mapped to mechanism_failure (R5 judgement). [date from report Date & Time field; Columbus, Georgia]

[family: Homebuilt (One Easy)] Video: right side of canopy bouncing slightly open during taxi; witness saw canopy open during takeoff; erratic flight and turn-back; fire. PC: loss of control due to diverted attention to the canopy opening. Lock not examinable (fire); evidence suggests not latched (R5 note, not an NTSB finding). [date from report Date & Time field; Battle Creek, Michigan]

[family: Thorp T-18] In initial climb the canopy partially disconnected (aft retaining/slide mechanism separated at a weld), violent vibration; precautionary landing hit fence post. Failure mode undetermined; possibly repeated loading. Partial separation coded canopy_departed. [date from report Date & Time field; Independence, Oregon]

[family: Homebuilt (JSX-2)] Canopy opened after takeoff; aircraft very hard to control (pitching, yawing); hard landing, gear collapse. PC: failure to ensure canopy properly secured before takeoff. [date from report Date & Time field; Chesterfield, Missouri]

[family: Schempp-Hirth Ventus] Canopy opened on tow; opened again on final with airbrakes; hit shipping container. PC: failure to properly secure canopy before flight. [date from report Date & Time field; Wurtsboro, New York]

[family: Grob G103] Rear canopy opened on aerotow near 3,000 ft AGL and then separated; tow rope failed and lodged in rudder; hard landing. Contributing: failure to properly secure the aft canopy. [date from report Date & Time field; San Antonio, Texas]

[family: Grumman AA-1] Sliding canopy, pilot habitually flew with it partly open for cooling (placard allows half-open); canopy moved fully open in flight; screw-knob lock found mostly unscrewed; stall/spin. PC: canopy moving fully open causing distraction. Intermediate-position mode coded partially_latched (R5). [date from report Date & Time field; Cleburne, Texas]

aircraft_type: CZECH SPORT AIRCRAFT AS PIPER SPORT
notes: [family: Czech Sportcruiser] Piper Sport: solo student found at ~250 ft AGL that the canopy was unlocked; returned to land; improper flare, nose-down runway impact. Report does not say canopy opened (event=other). [date from report Date & Time field; Santa Monica, California]

[family: Vans RV] Canopy fell in a yard 1.5 mi from wreckage; handle found open, locking pin bent. PC: failure to properly secure the canopy before takeoff, allowing it to open and separate in flight; loss of control. [date from report Date & Time field; Chattahoochee, Florida]

[family: Schempp-Hirth Discus] At 3,700 ft MSL canopy suddenly separated. Cracks from a stop-drilled hole progressed. PC: improper crack repair by maintenance. (Also listed in BFU Bulletin 10/2022 as BFU22-1136-DX.) [date from report Date & Time field; Woodstock, Virginia]

[family: Homebuilt (Gleim MG-1)] Canopy suddenly opened in level flight; emergency landing on dirt road; loss of directional control. Lock state not stated. [date from report Date & Time field; Madera, California]

[family: Rutan EZ] Berkut 540: canopy departed shortly after takeoff. PC: failure to verify the canopy latches were in the locked position before takeoff (pilot: both handles should have been checked). [date from report Date & Time field; Orlando, Florida]

aircraft_type: BURKHART GROB LUFT UND RAUMFAH G103 TWIN ASTIR TRAI
notes: [family: Grob G103] Rear canopy opened very early in aerotow; instructor said he likely did not properly close and lock it; off-airport landing in corn field. PC: failure to properly lock the rear canopy. [date from report Date & Time field; Brownsboro, Alabama]

[family: Extra] Pilot thought he had closed and locked the canopy but did not push up on it as usual; canopy opened shortly after start of takeoff roll and struck right wing. PC: failure to ensure canopy properly locked. [date from report Date & Time field; Whitehouse, Ohio]

[family: SZD Foka] Bicester. FIRST flight of the day: as airbrakes were extended on final, canopy opened and slid forward on its rails; pilot held it with one hand and landed. Owner suggested link with airbrake opening. The later fatal flight the same day was a rigging accident; that outcome is NOT this row's outcome.

[family: Grob G103] Saint-Affrique. Rear canopy opened at a few metres on aerotow; pilot (first time in rear seat) thinks he did not lock it completely despite a mnemonic; distracted by tug pilot helping passenger; late release, failed turn-back. Lock system found serviceable. Injuries not stated in report ('fortement endommage' mapped substantial).

[family: Cap 10] Martinique. Canopy opened during aerobatic training; passenger held it for landing. Rear canopy attachment pin found out of its housing; BEA: an unintended action on the red jettison handle (no safety wire, near the lock handle) may have released it (possible, not certain). Page read via WebFetch summary.

[family: Cap 10] Chavenay. Canopy opened in transit to aerobatic area and separated, struck right wing and tailplane. Rear-left lock not engaged on its lug; canopy frame easily deformed so lock can look closed; correct locking hard to see (behind pilot's left shoulder). Cause: insufficient check of canopy locking before takeoff. Family Cap (CAP 20 is the predecessor of Cap 10/20/230 line). Page read via WebFetch summary.

[family: Microlight (other)] Forward-tilting canopy opened at 5-10 m during acceleration after liftoff; elevator seemed ineffective; hard landing. Lock system found serviceable; BEA: pilot's visual check probably did not detect that the locking lug was not engaged; suction over fuselage initiated opening. 'Important' damage mapped substantial. Page read via WebFetch summary.

[family: Czech Sportcruiser] Muret. Rear-left latch not engaged (canopy poorly fitted); instructor had student unlock canopy in flight to relatch it; canopy lifted, nose-down pitch, jacket caught on stabiliser. Cockpit switch senses the LEVER position, not the latches, so the partial lock gave no alarm. WARNING FITTED BUT DID NOT DETECT.

[family: Grob G103] Lyon-Corbas. Instructor's (rear) canopy opened abruptly seconds after aerotow liftoff; student lost tow position and released; landing in trees. Cause of opening not established; BEA: each occupant must check his own canopy. Page read via WebFetch summary.

[family: Schleicher ASK] Le Havre Saint-Romain. Canopy opened fully at ~10 m, 25 s after wheels-off on aerotow (solo student); student tried to close it while releasing stick; high position, tug released; stall in turn-back. Video shows canopy not locked; BEA: probably inadequate locking before takeoff (probable, so unknown per R2 rule). No training item on canopy opening.

[family: Robin] Saint-Remy-de-Maurienne. At takeoff the central canopy-door hook was incorrectly locked; doors gaped ~5 cm; pilot chose not to relatch and continued; tailwind landing, runway excursion. Category 3 (pilot testimony). Page read via WebFetch summary.

[family: Cap 232] Chavenay-Villepreux. Pilot left canopy locked in the ajar (ventilation) position for taxi because of heat and took off so; when he unlocked it in flight to close it, it opened fully and was torn off; no wind protection, poor visual references, CFIT short of runway 28. Same 'intermediate position' failure mode as AAIB G-GODV.

[family: Schempp-Hirth Ventus] Serres-La-Batie. Canopy opened unexpectedly shortly after takeoff; plexiglass separated from frame and struck the propeller; turn-back, trees. Investigation in progress (50%); no cause yet. Page read via WebFetch summary.

aircraft_type: Grob G 103 C Twin III Acro
notes: [family: Grob G103] Eschwege-Stauffenbuehl. Passenger video shows front-canopy lock lever vertical (unlocked) before and during the winch launch; canopy opened on final at ~30 m AGL; pilot tried to hold/close it, steep descent, impact; 2 fatal. AFM: both locks to be checked before each flight. Facts-only report (no analysis).

[family: Grob G103] Kempten. Rear canopy opened for unknown reasons during aerotow start; takeoff abandoned, rope released; tree contact during turn-back; both occupants seriously injured. Only the BFU short summary was read; no per-case report located.
[family: Schleicher ASW] Aukrug. Canopy came loose ('loeste sich') in initial climb of a winch launch; left wing, tailplane and fin damaged, canopy destroyed. BFU short summary only.
[family: Grob G103] Muensingen-Eisberg. Rear canopy opened during winch launch; solo student underflew the winch cable, which wrapped the right wing; landed. BFU short summary only.
[family: Grob G103] Bamberg. Canopy opened unintentionally in flight; subsequent outlanding overran into a car-park fence. Different event from 3X081-99 on the same date. BFU short summary only.
[family: Grob G102] Strausberg. Glider lost its canopy during winch launch; canopy struck the tail; landed without problems. BFU short summary only.
[family: Schleicher ASK] Heppenheim. Canopy opened during takeoff ('Im Start'); hard ground contact; fatal. BFU short summary only.
[family: LET Blanik] Pinnow. Motorglider lost its canopy during the takeoff roll; canopy, its hinge, fuselage and left tailplane damaged. BFU short summary only.
[family: Schempp-Hirth Nimbus] Heppenheim. Canopy opened during aerotow start; after an undulating final approach, hard touchdown broke both wings. BFU short summary only.
[family: Grob G109] Lahr. Right cockpit door (canopy door) opened in initial climb; motorglider crashed onto the airfield during the turn-back. BFU short summary only.
[family: Ikarus C42] Lauenbrueck. Cabin door opened shortly after liftoff; climb could not be continued; impact from ~10 m, fire. BFU short summary only.
[family: Grob G102] Hornberg. During the initial aerotow ground run pilot noticed canopy opening; aborted; ground loop. BFU short summary only.
[family: Schleicher ASK] Koenigsdorf. Canopy opened on aerotow (dual training); hard outlanding; serious injury. BFU short summary only.

[family: Letov L-33] Radevormwald-Leye. On aerotow the airbrakes were fully extended AND the canopy was not locked; tow released at ~30 m; landed beside runway. Summary does not say whether the canopy opened (event=other).

[family: SZD Bocian] EPBA. Winch launch, ~50 m: rear canopy opened and fell off; instructor said it was closed and locked. Lock-knob spring force much lower than on other Bocians; a hard bounce during the ground run probably unlocked the weakly sprung knob. Glider undamaged (canopy lost: minor).

[family: Evektor Sportstar] EPSK (Czech-registered UL). Canopy opened at ~10 m after liftoff; pilot held it, instructor landed. Most probable cause: incomplete closure of lock mechanism unnoticed by crew (probable -> unknown per R2 rule). PKBWL comment: openings on forward-opening Zodiac/Sportstar-type canopies 'quite frequent'; nose-down tendency; nearly impossible to close in flight. AFM had no procedure.

[family: Pipistrel] EPBA training circuit, ~300 m AGL, 150 km/h: left (student) door opened, most of it fell off. Cockpit video: left handle CLOSED but not SECURED (not over dead-centre); bolts gradually backed out over the series of flights. Recommendation to manufacturer.

[family: XtremeAir] EPBC. During climb after takeoff canopy opened dynamically by itself, broke off its hinges and fell; headset torn off, no radio; landed after small circuit; marks on right wing and aileron. Cause: canopy lock unlocked in flight for undetermined reason.

[family: SZD Perkoz] EPBP. Sightseeing flight with passenger; during a sideslip on approach at ~50 m the canopy opened by itself and tore off, hitting right wing leading edge. Cause not determined; measure: ground crew must check passenger-seat canopy lock.

[family: SZD Bocian] EPBY. On downwind-landing approach at ~20 m front canopy opened and was torn away. Cause: improper closing of the front canopy by the student. Header date 14 Aug 2019; narrative says 16.08.2019 (date discrepancy in report).

[family: Extra] Second SP-HMM event (R2 row is 2022-03-18). After several aileron rolls, in level flight, canopy opened; retaining strap broke and canopy struck right wing; emergency landing. Causes (with BFU and Extra): lock design did not exclude partial locking when the rear slider handle was not in the placarded 'locked' position; locks may not have been fully locked before flight; suction and vibration at high speed drove partly engaged locks toward open. Damage: 'uszkodzony' (degree not stated).
[family: SZD Bocian] EPWS. Winch launch, entering steep climb: rear canopy opened (slid out) and fell. Cause: fractured spring that presses the rear-canopy lock; contributing: rough grass surface.
